messages.author: c454b293eaa50635
messages.subject: Model superensemble
parts:
Hello,

I have a selection of 5 competing spatio-temporal negative binomial models. I would like to create a superensemble by combining the outputs of these competing models as in this paper: https://royalsocietypublishing.org/doi/full/10.1098/rsif.2016.0410 

Is this possible in INLA? I have looked at the INLABMA package but that does not do what I require.

Thanks in advance,
Felipe

messages.author: d560d9e01924933c
messages.subject: Re: [r-inla] Model superensemble
parts:
Hi Felipe,

I think you should try inla.merge.

?INLA::inla.merge

You can even add weights for each model, not sure how to do it though,
using normalized information criteria (WAIC or DIC)?

Cheers,
Leo

messages.author: 334c7505e0b5cf65
messages.subject: Re: [r-inla] Model superensemble
parts: Hi,

?INLA::inla.merge

You can even add weights for each model, not sure how to do it though,
using normalized information criteria (WAIC or DIC)?

Please, do not do that… In a Bayesian framework, use the marginal likelihood to weight models. See, for example, 

https://arxiv.org/abs/1911.00797


Best,

Virgilio

messages.author: 334c7505e0b5cf65
messages.subject: Re: [r-inla] Model superensemble
parts: Hi,

> What should be avoided the inla.merge or the weights using information
> criteria? I can see the later may be bad, but is there any issue on
> the inla.merge?

Weighting using the DIC or WAIC is not the right way to weight models in a Bayesian framework. Using inla.merge is fine and, actually, I have used in the link that I sent before.

Best,

Virgilio

messages.subject: Re: [r-inla] Re: Model superensemble
parts:
good question. I recall doing quite some work to get it where it is
today. the slow part is the merging of the marginal distributions for
the latent field.

like if you do not need them, you can do like this


> a=Sys.time(); rr = inla.merge(list(r,r,r,r,r,r,r,r,r,r));
print(Sys.time() - a)

Time difference of 3.449188232 secs


> r$marginals.random=NULL
> a=Sys.time(); rr = inla.merge(list(r,r,r,r,r,r,r,r,r,r));
print(Sys.time() - a)

Time difference of 0.1412577629 secs

messages.author: 334c7505e0b5cf65
messages.subject: Re: [r-inla] Model superensemble
parts:
Hi,

Also, in the INLABMA (on CRAN) there are functions to compute the weighted sum of a list of marginals. So, you can extract the marginals of the parameters from the inla objects and average them. Maybe that can be of help too. This will allow you to focus on the effects/hyperparameters that you need.

Best,

Virgilio
